subject: SDK caller-id propagation request (ACME) - header being dropped in streaming
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: runtime-team@redwood.com; platform-infra@redwood.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: SDK caller-id propagation request (ACME) - header being dropped in streaming

Team —

We have a P0 from ACME (deal ACME-3321). They require a stable per-customer caller id (they call it x-acme-client-id, but we're proposing we support X-Redwood-Caller-Id) that must travel from the SDK through our API to the runtime layer so that downstream routing and per-customer quotas/billing are correct.

Symptoms reported by ACME: when doing longer streaming sessions (~>20s), the caller-id header sometimes disappears and the request lands on the default tenant routing, causing mis-billing and occasional model fallback. Their security team has also flagged the inconsistency.

Ask: can runtime/proxy guarantee that an opaque header (X-Redwood-Caller-Id) included by the SDK is preserved end-to-end for both unary and streaming requests? If not, what is the minimal changeset to provide a guaranteed path for this metadata (SDK->edge->router->runtime)?

Attachments: callerid-spec.pdf (simple spec ACME provided) and a short repro summary from their side.

Constraints: ACME is asking for a timeline because they will not sign GTC until this is resolved. Sales/CS are pressing for a short-term mitigation we can ship ASAP (2-week target) and a longer-term robust solution.

Can runtime/edge team pick an owner and confirm:
- quick root cause hypothesis
- whether the header is explicitly stripped anywhere today (edge proxies, gateways, or req transforms)
- estimated ETA for a fix and whether it needs SDK change, infra change, or both

Thanks —
Olga
Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, runtime-team@redwood.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK caller-id propagation request (ACME) - header being dropped in streaming

Olga — thanks for the clear ticket and attachments. Quick summary from our side after a first-pass investigation:

- Reproducer looks plausible: we found a case where the header is present on the initial HTTP/1.1 upgrade request but is dropped during chunked transfer handling between the edge proxy and the router when the connection is long-lived. This appears in our tracing where the initial request shows X-Redwood-Caller-Id, but downstream grpc metadata sections do not.

- Root cause hypothesis: our edge proxy library sanitizes certain headers during connection upgrades and chunk processing; there is an allowed-list for headers forwarded as grpc metadata and X-Redwood-Caller-Id is not on it. The behavior is different between unary and streaming flows which is why ACME sees intermittent issues.

Short-term mitigations we can consider (quick to implement):
1) Add X-Redwood-Caller-Id to the edge proxy forward list (config change + small patch) — low risk, can be canaried.
2) SDK fallback: include caller id also as a query param (e.g. ?caller_id=) for streaming endpoints — lower SLO impact but messy from a security standpoint (exposes in logs). Requires coordination with SDK teams.
3) Router rule override: for ACME only, route on source IP or api-key if caller id missing — brittle and not ideal.

We need a short reproducer with a trace-id that shows the header on the inbound request but not on the runtime. Olga — can you forward the trace snippet or an approximate curl/websocket sequence from ACME? I attached a short trace extraction (edge-trace-sample.txt) with the headers we saw in staging.

ETA estimation: if we go with (1) + a small SDK advisory to set the header in metadata, we can produce a canary in ~5 business days (patch -> internal canary -> canary rollback window) and full rollout in 10 business days. If we need protocol-level changes (gRPC metadata handling), add 2–3 weeks.

I'll pick up owner for the edge patch; need SDK lead to coordinate changes to the JS/Python SDKs.

— Dev
Platform Infra | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK caller-id propagation request (ACME) - header being dropped in streaming

Dev — thanks, that matches what ACME observed. Forwarding the repro they sent (included below). Paul, attaching the direct trace they captured (acme-repro-logs.txt) — it includes request/response headers and the SDK timing.

ACME reproducer (from their notes):
1) Start a JS streaming session using our /v1/stream endpoint with header X-Redwood-Caller-Id: \"acme-nyc-74\"
2) Send several payload chunks over ~30s (they used a 10KB chunk every 3s)
3) Observe the server-side routing logs: after ~15–20s some requests show up without caller id in runtime logs and fall back to the default route.

Paul (ACME) — can you add the trace id from the logs when you see the fallback? That will help us pin down the exact proxy hop.

From a prioritization perspective: ACME is holding paperwork until we can show a fix plan. They prefer not to have caller id in query params. Short-term they want the edge config change + a canary. They also asked whether Dedicated/Private deployments see the same issue — if the bug lives in the common edge library, it likely affects all modes.

Next asks for runtime/edge:
- confirm whether adding the header to forward-list is purely config or requires a code change in the proxy library
- confirm whether we need SDK advisory (we'll draft messaging once you confirm)
- rough ETA for canary (we're aiming for <2 weeks)

Olga
Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Looping in with a proposed execution plan and owners so sales has something concrete to present to ACME tomorrow: 

1) Hotfix (P0) — Edge proxy forward-list addition
   - Owner: Dev Patel (infra)
   - Work: add X-Redwood-Caller-Id to the allowed header forward-list and ensure transformation to gRPC metadata for streaming. Quick unit test + staging canary.
   - ETA: 5 business days to internal canary, 10 business days to full rollout (if canary acceptable).

2) SDK advisory + optional change (P1)
   - Owner: Marissa Cole (SDK lead)
   - Work: publish advisory that SDKs should set caller id in streaming metadata (JS/Python). If acceptable, include optional SDK patch to explicitly set metadata field and a small integration test to avoid regressions.
   - ETA: advisory out in 48 hours; SDK patches in ~7 business days.

3) Dedicated/Private verification (P0)
   - Owner: Karthik Iyer (runtime)
   - Work: verify whether private deployments using older edge libs are affected; if yes, coordinate backport plan with CS/ops.
   - ETA: verification in 48 hours, backport plan if needed within 3 business days.

Action items for Olga/Marissa:
- Olga: get any additional trace-ids from ACME (they promised one per fallback event). Put them in this thread.
- Marissa: if you can draft the advisory copy we can include it with the canary notes.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with Dev + Marissa + Olga tomorrow to review the canary plan and the rollout gating criteria (error rates, header-presence metric, latency).

Karthik
Engineering Manager, Runtime | Redwood Inference
